prompt: Design the first screen of a landing page for Quarry, a tool that turns meeting recordings into searchable notes. Include the product name, a headline, one supporting sentence, a primary button to start a free trial, a secondary link to watch a demo, and a simple product preview made with CSS. Return a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts only, and no external assets or scripts. The important content must be visible in the first 1280x800 viewport.
rubric: One element (the headline or the preview) is clearly the focal point when the page is blurred or squinted at.
The free-trial button is visibly dominant over the demo link, which is clearly quieter.
The supporting sentence and product name sit clearly below the headline in size or weight, with a visible step between levels.
Text and controls share consistent edges; a headline is not centered over flush-left text.
No decorative gradients, glows, glass panels, or blobs compete with the headline or the button.

prompt: Our account settings page has these properties: section titles are 15px and body text is 14px, every row uses the same weight, there are three solid blue buttons in the footer (Save, Reset, Export), helper text is light gray at 12px, and every group of settings sits inside its own bordered box. Critique the visual hierarchy and list fixes in priority order.
rubric: Identifies that the step between section titles and body text is too small and proposes a clearly larger or heavier title.
Identifies that three equally loud buttons compete and proposes one primary with quieter secondaries.
Suggests replacing some of the boxes with space or stronger section headings.
Flags the light gray helper text as a legibility risk rather than only as a hierarchy tool.
Orders the fixes by impact on the user's task.
The price is the dominant element within each card, clearly larger or heavier than the feature lines.
The recommended plan is marked by a label and structural emphasis, not by color alone.
The per-feature badges and heavy background effects are reduced or removed.
Card edges, baselines and the button positions are aligned across the three plans.
Button styling follows plan rank, not three equally loud buttons; all original text is kept.

prompt: An account page must make clear that the customer's card will be charged tomorrow. The options are: a red banner across the top of every page, a bold line beside the plan name, a modal that opens on page load, or a small icon plus a bold sentence in the billing section. Pick one and justify it in under 120 words.
rubric: Picks a proportionate, in-context option such as the billing-section notice, or a quiet top notice if urgency truly demands it.
Rejects or argues against the modal that opens on page load.
Mentions a cue that does not rely on color alone, such as an icon or text.
Explains that the notice should sit near the related billing content.
Stays within about 120 words.

prompt: Define the levels of hierarchy and the treatment of each for a long-form article page. The content is: title, standfirst, byline, date, body text, subheads, pull quotes, and related links.
rubric: Defines three or four levels and gives a reason for each placement.
Places byline and date at a quiet meta level rather than competing with the title.
Makes pull quotes distinct without outranking the title.
Treats related links as subordinate to the article body.
Changes roughly one visual variable per level, and states what that variable is.

prompt: Explain to a junior designer why making every important label bold weakens a page. Keep it under 120 words.
rubric: Explains that emphasis works only as a difference relative to its surroundings.
Mentions limiting the share of emphasized items, or an emphasis budget.
Offers alternatives such as space, position, or one consistent technique.
Is concise and stays under about 120 words.

prompt: Design the empty state for the project list in a task app: a short explanation of what projects are, a button to create the first project, and a small help link to a guide. Return a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts only, and no external assets or scripts. The important content must be visible in the first 1280x800 viewport.
rubric: There is one clear focal message when the page is blurred.
There is a single primary action and it is visibly the strongest control.
Any illustration or icon is small and subordinate to the message and button.
The help link is clearly quieter than the primary button.
No competing decoration such as glows, heavy gradients, or extra boxes.

prompt: Build a table of 12 invoices with invoice number, client, date, amount, and status (paid, due, overdue). Use made-up data. Return a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts only, and no external assets or scripts. The important content must be visible in the first 1280x800 viewport.
rubric: Amounts are aligned so that they can be compared, for example right-aligned with consistent decimals.
Status is readable as text and not only by color.
The header row is distinguishable but quiet, not louder than the data.
Rows are not decorated with extra emphasis, badges, or boxes beyond what scanning needs.
Overall the table is clean and readable at the viewport.

prompt: Design a formal wedding invitation shown as a single centered card: the couple's names, date, venue, and an RSVP line. Use made-up names. Return a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, system fonts only, and no external assets or scripts. The important content must be visible in the first 1280x800 viewport.
rubric: The composition is symmetric and centered as requested.
There is a clear order: names first, then date, then venue, then RSVP.
Ornament is restrained and does not overpower the names.
It does not force flush-left alignment or an asymmetric layout against the request.

prompt: Our trading blotter shows 40 rows of numbers that traders watch all day. A designer wants to make it airier with bigger headings and fewer visible rows. Advise.
rubric: Keeps the density that continuous monitoring needs instead of simply enlarging everything.
Proposes hierarchy through alignment, weight, and value rather than through larger type.
Keeps one clear focus, such as exceptions or alerts.
Pushes back on cutting visible rows unless there is a task reason, and suggests how to check that.
